idiom_name: lapin Channel::basic_consume -> Consumer stream with explicit acks
implementation_notes: lapin provides the endpoint machinery for AMQP 0-9-1: after creating a Connection and Channel, basic_consume() returns a Consumer that is an async Stream of message::Delivery, so the endpoint loop is 'while let Some(delivery) = consumer.next().await' with delivery.ack(BasicAckOptions::default()).await. The library also offers automatic connection recovery (ConnectionProperties::enable_auto_recover plus wait_for_recovery), which replays topology and consumers; rdkafka's StreamConsumer is the Kafka analogue. The classic endpoint type is still worth writing for lifecycle, decoding and error policy.
pitfalls: Dropping the Consumer cancels consumption: it must be kept alive in the endpoint (or re-created after errors), and recovery only replays consumers if auto-recovery was enabled before the failure.
Deliveries must be acked or rejected exactly once; leaking an unacked delivery eats the broker's prefetch window until the channel stalls.
An ack sent on a different channel than the delivery is a protocol error; keep the channel owned by the endpoint single-threaded.
